finding.claim: Unrestricted SSRF in /logo: the 'logo' parameter is only checked with a substring match for 'example.io', so any host, scheme (http/https), or path can be fetched, and the response body is returned to the caller.
finding.source: r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31 (attacker-controlled query/form parameter on GET /logo, listener :8081)
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, default client following up to 10 redirects; body returned via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only validation; substring match, not hostname match
http.Get(raw) fetches the full attacker-supplied URL, redirects followed
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) reflects the fetched body to the attacker (non-blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: Substring check at main.go:32 is bypassable: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io reaches cloud metadata; http://127.0.0.1:6379/?example.io reaches loopback; http://attacker.test/?example.io reaches arbitrary hosts; allowed hosts can 302 to internal addresses since redirects are not restricted. Non-http(s) schemes fail in http.Get and leave resp nil, causing a nil-deref panic at main.go:37 (reliability, not SSRF). Listener binds all interfaces (main.go:44), widening exposure.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the substring match `strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")` at main.go:32, which does not close the finding. The default http.Get at main.go:36 follows redirects, and the body is copied to the response at main.go:38.
verdict.reason: The `logo` value comes straight from `r.FormValue("logo")` at main.go:31, the substring check at main.go:32 is the only validation, and `http.Get(raw)` at main.go:36 fetches an attacker-chosen URL whose body is returned via `io.Copy` at main.go:38, so this is a non-blind SSRF. The trace matches the code, and the nil-deref note at main.go:36-37 also holds because `resp` is nil when `http.Get` fails on a non-http(s) scheme.

finding.claim: Not a finding: /cdn is protected by an exact Hostname() allowlist (cdn.example.io) and blocks redirects, so attacker cannot reach arbitrary or internal hosts via this handler.

noRedirect returns http.ErrUseLastResponse, blocking redirect-based pivots

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allowlist, redirect blocking. Residual risk limited to DNS control of cdn.example.io, which is not attacker-controlled. Note: err from c.Get ignored at main.go:25, nil-deref panic at main.go:26 on failure (reliability, not SSRF).

verdict.guard_found: main.go:20 `trusted[u.Hostname()]` is an exact, case-sensitive map-membership check on the parsed hostname against {"cdn.example.io"}. Redirects are also blocked by main.go:12 (`http.ErrUseLastResponse`) and wired in at main.go:24.
verdict.reason: The source at main.go:15 is attacker-controlled, but the exact `Hostname()` membership check at main.go:20 closes the SSRF path, and the redirect block at main.go:12/24 stops pivots. The sink at main.go:25 uses the same parsed URL that passed the check, so the request can only reach cdn.example.io. Every trace line matches the code. The nil-deref at main.go:26 on error is a reliability bug, not SSRF.
